skill.name: migrate-radix-to-base
skill.description: Migrates React projects and components from Radix UI to Base UI. Use when asked to migrate from radix, move to base-ui, convert radix primitives, or switch a shadcn project's base library. Handles single components ("migrate accordion") and whole projects.
skill.summary: Guides safe, verifiable migrations from Radix UI components to Base UI.
skill.author: shadcn-ui

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, credential access, exfiltration intent, or malicious system discovery was found. Most alerts are Markdown formatting false positives, while the unpinned npx command, file-changing commands, and remote registry fetches present legitimate migration risks.

remediation.issue: The preflight runs shadcn through npx with the mutable latest tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited shadcn CLI version and require user confirmation before downloading or executing it.

remediation.issue: The workflow can overwrite or merge project files through external commands.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact target files, confirm a clean branch, and request approval before overwrite or in-place merge operations.

remediation.issue: Migration source files are fetched from a mutable remote registry.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict requests to the documented HTTPS host, validate responses, and review diffs before applying fetched content.

content.user_title: Migrate Radix UI Projects to Base UI
content.value_statement: Radix-to-Base migrations can break wrapper behavior, styles, and consumer props. This skill applies component mappings, progressive workflows, verification, and migration reports.
actual_capabilities: Classifies shadcn wrappers as pristine or customized before migration.
Migrates one component progressively or processes an explicitly requested whole project.
Maps Radix parts, props, data attributes, CSS variables, and consumer call sites to Base UI.
Preserves customized wrappers through golden-pair comparison and three-way merge guidance.
Runs typechecks and builds, then records component-specific migration reports.
limitations: It requires installed project dependencies and access to local Base UI type declarations.
Legacy shadcn styles have no matching Base UI registry variant.
Behavior differences still require manual testing for focus, keyboard navigation, delays, and events.
It does not migrate unrelated libraries such as cmdk, vaul, sonner, or react-day-picker.

use_cases.title: Migrate one wrapper safely
use_cases.description: Move a single customized component to Base UI while preserving its existing Radix implementation until consumers are updated.

use_cases.title: Convert a component library
use_cases.description: Migrate shared wrappers in dependency order and track remaining Radix imports across an application.

use_cases.title: Plan a repository migration
use_cases.description: Assess wrappers, dependencies, consumer changes, and verification work before a complete Base UI transition.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate one component
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate the accordion component from Radix UI to Base UI. Preserve custom styles, update consumers, typecheck changes, and create the migration report.

prompt_templates.title: Resume progressive migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume the existing progressive migration for select. Inspect current Base variants and consumer imports before making the next safe change.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate customized wrappers
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate dialog and dropdown-menu wrappers. Compare each wrapper with its registry origin, preserve customizations, update call sites, and report behavior changes.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate the whole project
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate this entire project from Radix UI to Base UI. Process wrappers by dependency order, sweep application code, verify builds, and summarize remaining risks.

output_examples.output: Accordion migrated through a progressive Base UI variant. Consumer imports were updated, typechecks passed, and no Radix wrappers remain for this component.

output: Compared the wrapper with its Radix registry origin.
Preserved local classes while replacing Radix primitives and props.
Flagged focus-return behavior for manual verification.

output_examples.input: What remains in the project migration?
output_examples.output: The report identifies remaining Radix wrappers, unresolved behavior differences, dependency cleanup, and the latest build result.

best_practices: Start from a clean branch and record the baseline typecheck or build result.
Migrate dependency wrappers before components that consume them.
Review each diff and manually test keyboard, focus, and event behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not overwrite every registry component in one command.
Do not remove Radix packages before the final dependent wrapper is migrated.
Do not treat a clean merge or successful typecheck as complete behavior validation.

faq.question: Can it migrate one component?
faq.answer: Yes. Progressive mode creates a Base variant, updates consumers individually, and keeps the original until migration is complete.

faq.question: Can it migrate a whole project?
faq.answer: Yes, when explicitly requested. It processes wrappers in dependency order, updates application code, removes dependencies, and runs a final build.

faq.question: Does it preserve custom styling?
faq.answer: It compares customized wrappers with registry versions and replays local differences onto the Base variant.

faq.question: Does it support legacy shadcn styles?
faq.answer: Yes, with limits. It transforms the existing files directly because legacy styles do not have matching Base registry variants.

faq.question: What verification does it perform?
faq.answer: It uses per-file typechecks, batch builds, final builds, leftover import scans, and manual behavior checklists.

faq.question: Does it migrate every UI library?
faq.answer: No. It leaves unrelated libraries and wrappers unchanged, including cmdk, vaul, sonner, input-otp, react-day-picker, and recharts.
